feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear domain focus, solid progression, and relevant public-sector scale. It reads polished and substantive, but it is slightly dense and somewhat repetitive across summary, skills, projects, and experience, which reduces impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong career progression at NACo and a well-defined niche in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications systems.  
- Good use of scale and credibility markers: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms strengthen trust.  
- Writing is generally professional and error-free, with no obvious misspellings; tone is consistent and appropriate for senior-level roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” “Core Competencies,” and “Recent Projects” overlap heavily. Consolidating these sections would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities, especially for the freelance role and earlier positions; include measurable results where possible.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; date formatting varies slightly (“Oct.”/“Sept.”/“Mar.”); “English (Native)” and “French (A2/Learning)” would read more cleanly as “Native” and “A2 (learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with good scope and sector fit, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets. It would be stronger with sharper differentiation and a few concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and reduce repetition: replace “platforms, governance models and content operations” with a more concise phrase and avoid re-listing capabilities already covered in Core Competencies.
- Add scale or context from recent roles, e.g. “10,000+ page web ecosystems,” “50+ publishers,” or “high-volume member/public audiences.”
- Use a more direct opening tied to target roles: “Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years…”
- Possible rewrite: “Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years guiding web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Delivers scalable Drupal-based publishing ecosystems, editorial workflows, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled discovery experiences that improve usability, coordination, and audience reach.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; “AI-enabled discovery experiences” is more specific.
- The subtitle already signals leadership; avoid repeating “Senior digital leader” verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and with slightly tighter, more parallel wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more concise, parallel noun phrases; e.g. “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Tighten and modernize wording: “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure,” “AI-enabled search and content discovery.”
- Consider grouping adjacent ideas to reduce sprawl: “Workflow automation, platform integration, and content operations.”
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills blocks.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is already well established in the header and work experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening the language and emphasizing outcomes, scope, or distinct formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/launched X using Y to achieve Z.”
- Replace generic phrases like “improve discovery” or “designed for continued campaign growth” with clearer outcomes if available (for example: faster access, reusable campaign framework, expanded engagement).
- Standardize style and punctuation: use sentence case, include the multiplication sign consistently as “10 × 20-foot,” and consider “AI-powered” instead of “AI-enabled” for variety.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and the microsite closely overlap with the current freelance role; make sure the footer adds specificity not already stated there.
- Advocacy Video Series overlaps with multiple NACo roles; consider reframing it around scale, format, or channel integration.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the “Recent Projects” section. Tighten it around leadership, platform modernization, and AI/search impact, with 1–2 concrete outcomes if available.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client context in one line: “Embedded as a full-time consultant supporting a U.S. national membership organization’s digital strategy, Drupal platform modernization, and communications operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets: combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one stronger bullet focused on organization-wide communications infrastructure.
- Rephrase for impact: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits” and “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and user discovery.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, publishers/users served, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search accuracy/engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current microsite and AI-search bullets duplicate the “Recent Projects” section; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the implementation detail.
- “Governance/usability/operational best practices” overlaps with prior NACo roles; make this version more specific to enterprise web improvement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize transformation outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in the earlier NACo role.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed enterprise digital strategy, platform operations, analytics, governance, and budget for NACo’s web, email, social, and video ecosystem.”
- Recast bullets around major wins, not channel oversight: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where missing: quantify newsletter growth/open rates, social engagement, video output, cost savings from the in-house studio, reporting efficiency, or governance adoption.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels...” with a results-focused bullet such as “Scaled email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials and improving campaign coordination across advocacy and member communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current email/social/video management language overlaps with the 2018–2022 NACo role.
- “Built first in-house video studio” may overlap with footer project examples; keep this version outcome-focused.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to executional leadership and channel growth, with clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy, program and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add outcome language where possible: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Make workflow/editorial bullets more concrete: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes and standardized publishing workflows, improving coordination, consistency and turnaround times.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helped improve…” is weak and repetitive with the Director role’s governance/workflow language; use stronger ownership or cut.
- Video/livestream language also appears in the earlier NACo role and footer project list; keep this version focused on scaling the recurring series, not general production.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize higher-level leadership strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, executive-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital strategy and modernization”
- Make governance/content ops more distinctive: “Editorial systems and governance” → “Content governance and editorial operations”
- Tighten channel leadership: “Multi-channel communications leadership” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”
- Consider revised set: “Enterprise digital strategy and modernization • Content governance and editorial operations • Cross-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Audience-centered content strategy”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and less differentiated than experience-based strengths like modernization, analytics, or AI-enabled content experiences.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s currently a mixed keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. Make it more selective and senior-level by emphasizing platforms and execution themes most tied to recent impact.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences
- Drop lower-priority or older tools unless they are target-role requirements: remove jQuery first; consider removing WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages from this topline section.
- Use broader, outcome-oriented phrasing over tool lists: “CMS modernization and migration” and “API and workflow integrations” read stronger than isolated platforms.
- Keep this section to 5–6 items max so it complements, rather than repeats, the detailed Technical + IT section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” and “workflow automation” already appear in Core Competencies.
- Platform/tool specifics are duplicated almost exactly in Technical + IT; keep the topline version more strategic.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize strategic application, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line: “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & optimization.”
- Use grouped phrasing: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic items with sharper business language: “KPI framework development,” “executive reporting,” “SEO and digital performance analysis”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity; KPI framework development, executive reporting, SEO and digital performance analysis.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep this version strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “Leadership reporting” is weaker than “executive reporting” and overlaps with “analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several work-experience bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery environments and operational scope rather than generic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Studio, Livestream & Hybrid Event Production”
- Replace with tighter, more specific bullets:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and virtual event delivery
- PTZ camera and in-house studio operations
- Hybrid event run-of-show and technical coordination
- If accurate, add scale/outcome language instead of generic terms, e.g. “multi-camera livestream delivery” or “broadcast-quality in-house studio production”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” is broad and repeats experience already shown in NACo roles; “broadcast-quality” or “studio-based” is more differentiated.
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies; use this section to specify formats/tools/workflows, not restate the same capability.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either be tightened for scannability or add light proficiency/context to reinforce recent Drupal-led work.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**.
- Add a qualifier only where it strengthens your current positioning: e.g. **Drupal (migration, governance, microsites)**.
- Keep this item platform-only; avoid mixing in modernization or technical execution terms already covered elsewhere.
- If space allows, use a label like **CMS & Web Platforms:** to make the section more purposeful.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or making this one shorter.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus your enterprise profile unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Tighten and modernize the list: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop jQuery unless it is still actively used in recent projects; it can date the profile and dilute stronger current tools
- If space allows, add one brief qualifier for impact/context, e.g. “for Drupal builds, analytics deployment, workflow automation, and lightweight edge/serverless functions”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; consider keeping detail here and shortening the Topline version
- “Workflow automation” is covered elsewhere, so avoid adding overlapping automation language in this item unless tied to GitHub Actions or Cloudflare Workers

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems
- Group by function to show judgment, not just familiarity: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add a qualifier for depth: “Workflow automation and team coordination tools” or “Built/managed workflows in…”
- Consider trimming older/basic collaboration tools if space is tight; keep the strongest signals for recent work: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira/Asana, Slack/Teams

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; listing both can dilute impact unless they were used for structured workflow orchestration.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Given the strong email leadership in recent NACo roles, this item should signal scale and purpose, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp — used to manage newsletter, campaign and member communications workflows**
- If accurate, add scope in a parenthetical: **(supporting newsletters and campaigns reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders)**
- Keep product names concise and standardized: use **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys** consistently; avoid slash-heavy formatting if space is tight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work experience bullets about leading email newsletters; don’t repeat audience scale here unless you remove or shorten similar wording elsewhere.
- “Engagement” may overlap with Higher Logic’s member/community use case; only keep that label if community/member engagement was a real part of your work.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is very close to the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills entry and reads as a generic keyword list. It should be tightened and differentiated toward hands-on platforms/methods rather than broader capability labels.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing
- Replace “SEO” with “Google Search Console” if you want this section to stay tool-focused; keep SEO in Topline Skills where it reads as a capability.
- Remove “Dashboarding” since reporting/dashboard infrastructure is already implied by Looker Studio and Power BI.
- Consider ordering by strongest/recently evidenced tools from the NACo role: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Power BI • Looker Studio • BigQuery • Google Search Console • A/B testing

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Keep one broader and one strictly tool-based.
- “SEO” also overlaps with “performance analysis” in Topline Skills.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete contributions and scale where possible: “Supported a major website refresh” → specify platform, launch, traffic, or content volume if known.
- Tighten the second sentence around outputs: “Produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video update, and helped standardize day-to-day digital publishing workflows.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: “provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate” → “coordinated daily work with/mentored a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or piloting the format.
- Avoid repeating governance/workflow language already used more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia and innovation work at NACo, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later digital/media roles. Tighten it to emphasize foundational impact—especially the first podcast launch—and any concrete outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the strongest achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with specific deliverables: multimedia assets, research briefs, program materials, or stakeholder-facing content.
- If possible, add scale or outcome: number of episodes, audiences served, teams supported, or how the podcast/content advanced member engagement or policy communications.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so the progression to digital leadership remains clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating generic multimedia/video language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; position it as a coordination/launch role that set up later advancement.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful supporting skills, but this item is a bit generic and overlaps with stronger multimedia claims already made in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize tools/software and keep workflow capabilities concise.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Creative Software & Production Tools”
- Rewrite as: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production workflows • Podcast recording and post-production”
- Use consistent software naming (add “Adobe” or remove it everywhere).
- If accurate, strengthen with specificity such as “multi-camera livestream production” or “audio editing and mastering” rather than broad “studio workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” and “Podcast production” repeat themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Avoid turning this into another summary of multimedia leadership; keep this item focused on hands-on tools and production capabilities.
